newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's CNMV approves Sefanitro bid.
newsitem.headline: Spain's CNMV approves Sefanitro bid.

text.p: Spain's stock market commission said on Thursday that it approved a takeover bid for chemicals firm Sefanitro by a group comprising six firms and individuals.

"The commission has authorised a bid made by Hydro Agri Espana SA, Berzeluis Felguera SA, Vicinay Cadenas SA, V.A.J. Investments, Jose Maria de la Iglesia Martinez and Carlos Castellanos Borresgo for 100 percent of Sefanitro's shares," the CNMV said in a press statement.
The commission said the offer was 600 pesetas per share for the company's 1.74 million shares.
The commission said the success of the bid would, however, depend on government approval since Sefanitro is a 52 percent unit of state holding company Agencia Industrial del Estado.
The CNMV previously authorised an initial offer by Fertiberia in October.
Sefanitro shares were suspended on November 12 after the CNMV received a competitive offer for the firm. Shares were trading at 625 pesetas prior to the suspension.
